title: City / Flow

benchmark.bar: Beat representative actual Cities: Skylines II gameplay at matched aerial/street views, resolution, scene scale and traffic density.
benchmark.reason: A fresh critic inspected the actual aerial, street, night and mobile captures beside the pinned Cities: Skylines II references. Repeated architectural massing and simplified foreground assets remain the largest visual gap. The commercial benchmark has not been met.

references.name: Cities: Skylines II
references.role: Main city, traffic and scene benchmark

checks.name: Production and browser authority compile
checks.detail: The same TypeScript simulation compiles for Node and browser ES modules.

checks.name: Local server and asset boundaries
checks.detail: 4 HTTP tests passed, including local Three.js assets, method rejection and repository path isolation.

checks.name: Deterministic traffic and dense intersections
checks.detail: Fresh critic independently closed the three original P1 defects. Quality remains in revision: fixed-ID corner allocation can repeatedly bypass older pedestrians; a fairness fix is underway.

checks.name: Integrated browser controls and recovery
checks.detail: All 8 Chromium checks passed on stable iteration 3: visible traffic, pause/speed, demand/policy/roadworks, cameras/night/overlay/sound, mobile targets and Escape, WebGL failure, actual context-loss recovery and live journal. Further vehicle, mobile queue-cue and pedestrian-fairness changes will receive affected checks.

checks.name: Unchanged catalogue baseline
checks.detail: Before feature changes, the baseline suite reported120 passed and3 failed: eko-run-headless, stream-host and candidate-script. This is not reported as a green full suite.

iterations.title: Repository baseline established
iterations.detail: Game 11 was present in the catalogue but had no dedicated implementation. The source snapshot was verified against 1,300 repository blob hashes.
findings: No traffic-game runtime to inspect at baseline.

iterations.title: First integrated city
iterations.detail: Independent builders implemented the traffic authority, city models and interface. The live build uses local assets and real simulation metrics.
findings: High-demand long-tail testing exposed gridlock after sustained operation.
External reference media remain unavailable.
changes: Connected road network, vehicle and pedestrian routes, junction reservations and signals.
Coastal district, dressed buildings, park, waterfront and animated agent models.
Working controls, camera modes, day/night presentation and optional sound.

iterations.title: Independent authority and rendering review
iterations.detail: Fresh headless probes reproduced failures that the initial builder tests missed. The actual browser reached its first rendered frame, but software-GPU throughput and screenshot capture were too slow.
findings: Citizens20 and30 occupied the same corner in a default seed2026 run at tick232.
A malformed restored completion history could inflate flow without completed trips.
A malformed restored reservation could admit a vehicle against the displayed green.
Actual first render reported238 calls and2,214,204 triangles;0.4fps on the shared software renderer, with interaction/capture timeouts.
changes: Entry metering and bounded rerouting closed the original high-demand gridlock regression.
iterations.verdict: REVISE — correctness and rendering fixes required

iterations.title: Commercial reference evidence retrieved
iterations.detail: The permitted network route made actual reference images available. The fixed benchmark now has inspected neighborhood and citizen/vehicle views; supporting streetscape and route-readability images are pinned too.
findings: Still images cannot establish motion, AI, audio or performance parity.
changes: Recorded original source URLs, dimensions, SHA-256 hashes and comparison limitations.

iterations.title: Real city captures complete
iterations.detail: The revised running build produced aerial, street, night and mobile screenshots without recorded browser errors. Captures use the actual application, paused through its operator command; desktop images are 1920×1080.
findings: Independent visual review still places the commercial reference ahead; repeated facades and simplified close assets are the next art gaps.
Paused screenshots do not prove a running frame-rate target.
changes: Distance detail preserves near models while reducing distant geometry.
Static shadow caching and on-demand paused rendering make capture and inspection practical.
First revised browser frame: 71 draw calls and 267,166 triangles at pixel ratio 1.
iterations.verdict: Captured — fresh critic review in progress

iterations.title: Fresh visual and interface verdicts
iterations.detail: Independent critics inspected the real captured city and pinned reference images. The commercial reference remains ahead; the next builder round follows the largest concrete gaps.
findings: Repeated box massing, window grids and roof rhythms dominate both aerial and street scenes.
The mobile HUD leaves too little unobstructed city; several touch targets are small.
The mobile queue legend disappears when Experiment is open.
Camera and night transitions stretched substantially under slow rendering.
changes: Returned architecture/frontage work to the world builder and mobile/control work to a separate UI builder.

iterations.title: UI critique reproduced in the running game
iterations.detail: Direct browser interaction confirmed the source-backed findings before revision.
findings: Changing speed while paused announced “Simulation running at 2× speed.”
The queue legend disappeared with the mobile Experiment panel open.
Escape from the focused demand slider did not close the panel.
changes: Recorded actual control bounds and mobile experiment screenshot.
Builder now has a concrete red case for each usability defect.

iterations.title: Architecture and phone layout improve
iterations.detail: A fresh critic chose the revised aerial image in a blind comparison before the iteration mapping was revealed. Both candidates were also compared directly with the pinned Cities reference. All six current captures have stable before/after source hashes.
findings: The commercial reference still leads. Near-camera cars, vans and buses are the largest next asset-quality gap.
Mobile city visibility is substantially improved, but the numerical queue cue can hide behind Experiment.
Default-demand pedestrian review found older corner requests repeatedly bypassed by lower-ID citizens, causing avoidable long stops.
changes: Added distinct arcade, stepped-apartment and commercial building families and connected the background district.
Condensed mobile HUD and enlarged principal touch controls; kept the queue legend in Experiment.
Corrected paused feedback and focused-control Escape handling; camera transitions now use presentation time.
iterations.verdict: Improved — continue with vehicle assets, queue readability and pedestrian fairness

next: Remove deterministic corner-allocation unfairness while retaining separation, valid restore and meaningful journey progress.
Improve near-camera moving and parked vehicles, then compare the actual result against the same fixed references.
Keep queue information visible during mobile experiments; verify all controls and recovery on the integrated revision.

tooling.builders: Separate simulation, world and UI agents
